transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because I just feel worn down almost all the time. It's like, even after a full night’s sleep, I still wake up tired. By the time I’ve handled work and tried to deal with the clutter around the house, I just... I have very little energy left for anything else.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day?

Yeah, most days. There’s just this... this low, gray mood kind of running in the background. I mean, I can still go to the lab and talk to people just fine, but I don’t really feel light or excited about things anymore. Like, I used to really enjoy baking, or checking the telescope, and now I just don't have that same feeling about them the way I used to.
How long have you been feeling this low?
Well, it's been a while. I think this low baseline has been going on since... shortly after we moved into the older house. So, that would be a little over two years ago now.
During these past two years, have you had a period of at least two months when your mood felt essentially back to normal?
No, not really. I mean, there are better days here and there, but I don't think I've had a whole two months where I just felt like my old self again. It's pretty much always just... there.
Have you been having trouble concentrating or making decisions lately?

Yeah, actually, I have. Um, tasks that used to be pretty straightforward and sequential for me—like revising a paragraph for a grant at work, or even just picking out materials for a repair around the house—they just take me a lot longer now. My mind just feels a bit slower, I guess. And I find myself second-guessing really small decisions that shouldn't be a big deal.
Have you ever had a distinct period of at least two weeks when your depression became noticeably worse than this usual low baseline?

No, I don't think so. It's just been this steady, low feeling the whole time. I haven't really had any periods where it suddenly got a lot worse for a couple of weeks or anything like that. It's just... consistently kind of gray.
